top_strength: The no-hidden-fees rundown was the best stretch of the call and he delivered it unprompted: "we don't have anything like a fuel fee. No disassemble, reassembly fees, no hidden fees of any type at all. It's just the hour the rate." His what's-included list was genuinely thorough too — gas, truck, supplies, taxes, insurance, tools for disassembly and reassembly, moving blankets and shrink wrap for fragile furniture. He also handled the clock mechanics cleanly, giving the 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute prorating and then proving it with a concrete example: if it only takes three hours, "You will only pay for three hours," and $714 for three and a half hours. He checked comprehension mid-pitch with "Do you have any questions about that so far?"
coaching_note: Jules, the one fix that would have changed this call is the estimate. She told you her dad is moving one apartment down the hall with "the bare minimum of stuff" and an empty second bedroom, and you handed her the generic one-bedroom number: six to seven hours. She said "Whoa" and left to shop. What that moment needed was: "Since this is down the hall and there's no truck load or drive time, this is nothing like a normal one-bedroom — those usually run six to seven hours, but a light room-to-room move like this is often closer to three or four. Let me ask a couple of things so I can tighten that up: what floor is he on, is there an elevator, and how long is the walk to the new unit?" Same honest range, anchored to her actual job instead of scaring her off it. Second priority: you never got her name or her email and you never asked for the business. You had confirmed availability in hand — that was your moment for "We do have September 1st open, and there's no deposit to hold it, so I can lock it in right now and email you the confirmation with everything in writing. Want me to?" Right now this lead is gone with no way to reach her. Third, small but costly: the three brand differentiators were all missing. No Worries Damage Coverage up to $2,000, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee are exactly what separate us from the other quotes she is about to collect — a price-shopper needs to hear them before she hangs up. One last thing: slow down on the pricing numbers. "Anywhere from like $10,100 and $90" cost you two rounds of back-and-forth on a simple question.
phone_presence_notes: He has surface affirmations ("Got it," "Exactly!", "Yeah, no problem," "sorry about that") but never learned or used the customer's name, and he walked past both emotional cues on the call — the elderly father downsizing into a smaller apartment, and her startled "Whoa" at the six-to-seven-hour estimate, which he answered with "Usually."
